title: Backend
body:
Everything that runs on the server: request routing, business logic, [[Authentication]] and [[Authorization]] checks, database access, background jobs. The kitchen and walk-in fridge — invisible to the guest, but what actually produces and stores everything the [[Frontend]] presents.

The client never sees this code, which is exactly why trust lives here: it's the only side of the split the user cannot modify. Backend work is typically split across several machines — an app server running [[Node.js]], [[Ruby on Rails]], or PHP, a separate database server, plus a [[Load Balancer]] in front. The boundary to the frontend is the [[API]], and being able to say *which* of these machines a given piece of logic belongs on is the skill the whole [[Web Interview Prep]] set is drilling.
